{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)

read_season <- function(file) {
  possible_paths <- c(
    file,
    paste0("data/", file),
    paste0("data/raw/", file),
    paste0("../data/", file),
    paste0("../data/raw/", file)
  )
  
  existing_path <- possible_paths[file.exists(possible_paths)][1]
  
  if (is.na(existing_path)) {
    stop(paste("File not found:", file))
  }
  
  read_csv(existing_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
}

s18 <- read_season("turkey-super-lig-teams-2018-to-2019-stats.csv")
s19 <- read_season("turkey-super-lig-teams-2019-to-2020-stats.csv")
s20 <- read_season("turkey-super-lig-teams-2020-to-2021-stats.csv")
s21 <- read_season("turkey-super-lig-teams-2021-to-2022-stats.csv")
s22 <- read_season("turkey-super-lig-teams-2022-to-2023-stats.csv")
s23 <- read_season("turkey-super-lig-teams-2023-to-2024-stats.csv")
s24 <- read_season("turkey-super-lig-teams-2024-to-2025-stats.csv")
s25 <- read_season("turkey-super-lig-teams-2025-to-2026-stats.csv")

superlig_data <- bind_rows(
  s18, s19, s20, s21,
  s22, s23, s24, s25
) %>%
  mutate(
    season_short = paste0(substr(season, 3, 4), "-", substr(season, 8, 9)),
    goals_minus_xg = goals_scored_per_match - xg_for_avg_overall,
    finishing_diff = goals_scored_per_match - xg_for_avg_overall,
    total_xg = xg_for_avg_overall * matches_played,
    shot_quality = total_xg / shots,
    shots_per_match = shots / matches_played,
    xg_per_shot = xg_for_avg_overall / shots_per_match
  )

Section 1 – Understanding Expected Goals and Match Performance

Expected Goals, commonly known as xG, is a football analytics metric that estimates the quality of chances created by a team. It does not directly measure the final score. Instead, it shows how many goals a team would be expected to score based on the quality of its chances.

In this section, we analyze how xG is related to different performance indicators in the Turkish Süper Lig.

1.1 Correlation Between xG and Performance Indicators

{r}
xg_correlations <- tibble::tibble(
  relationship = c(
    "xG vs Goals Scored",
    "xG vs Shots on Target",
    "xG vs Shots",
    "xG vs Points per Game"
  ),
  correlation = c(
    cor(superlig_data$xg_for_avg_overall, superlig_data$goals_scored_per_match, use = "complete.obs"),
    cor(superlig_data$xg_for_avg_overall, superlig_data$shots_on_target, use = "complete.obs"),
    cor(superlig_data$xg_for_avg_overall, superlig_data$shots, use = "complete.obs"),
    cor(superlig_data$xg_for_avg_overall, superlig_data$points_per_game, use = "complete.obs")
  )
)

xg_correlations

{r}
ggplot(xg_correlations, aes(x = reorder(relationship, correlation), y = correlation)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Which Performance Indicator is Most Related to xG?",
    x = "Relationship",
    y = "Correlation Coefficient"
  ) +
  ylim(0, 1) +
  theme_minimal()

The bar chart compares the strength of the relationship between xG and selected performance indicators. A higher correlation means that the variable has a stronger positive relationship with xG.

1.2 xG vs Goals Scored

{r}
cor_xg_goals <- cor(
  superlig_data$xg_for_avg_overall,
  superlig_data$goals_scored_per_match,
  use = "complete.obs"
)

cor_xg_goals

{r}
ggplot(
  superlig_data,
  aes(x = xg_for_avg_overall, y = goals_scored_per_match)
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "xG vs Goals Scored",
    subtitle = paste("Correlation:", round(cor_xg_goals, 3)),
    x = "Average xG per Match",
    y = "Average Goals Scored per Match"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

The scatter plot shows a positive relationship between xG and goals scored. Teams creating higher-quality chances generally score more goals. However, the relationship is not perfect because actual goals are affected by finishing quality, goalkeeper performance, defensive pressure, and randomness.

1.3 xG vs Shots on Target

{r}
cor_xg_sot <- cor(
  superlig_data$xg_for_avg_overall,
  superlig_data$shots_on_target,
  use = "complete.obs"
)

cor_xg_sot

{r}
ggplot(
  superlig_data,
  aes(x = xg_for_avg_overall, y = shots_on_target)
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "xG vs Shots on Target",
    subtitle = paste("Correlation:", round(cor_xg_sot, 3)),
    x = "Average xG per Match",
    y = "Shots on Target"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

A positive relationship is expected because teams that create more dangerous chances usually also record more shots on target.

1.4 xG vs Points per Game

{r}
cor_xg_points <- cor(
  superlig_data$xg_for_avg_overall,
  superlig_data$points_per_game,
  use = "complete.obs"
)

cor_xg_points

{r}
ggplot(
  superlig_data,
  aes(x = xg_for_avg_overall, y = points_per_game)
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "xG vs Points per Game",
    subtitle = paste("Correlation:", round(cor_xg_points, 3)),
    x = "Average xG per Match",
    y = "Points per Game"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

The relationship between xG and points per game may be weaker than xG and goals because points depend on both attacking and defensive performance.

1.5 xGA vs Goals Conceded

{r}
cor_xga_conceded <- cor(
  superlig_data$xg_against_avg_overall,
  superlig_data$goals_conceded_per_match,
  use = "complete.obs"
)

cor_xga_conceded

{r}
ggplot(
  superlig_data,
  aes(x = xg_against_avg_overall, y = goals_conceded_per_match)
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "xGA vs Goals Conceded",
    subtitle = paste("Correlation:", round(cor_xga_conceded, 3)),
    x = "Average xGA per Match",
    y = "Average Goals Conceded per Match"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

The defensive analysis shows whether expected goals against is related to actual goals conceded.

1.6 Why is the Correlation Not Equal to 1?

Although xG is related to goals and other performance indicators, the correlation is not expected to be exactly 1. This is because xG measures probability, not certainty.

{r}
ggplot(superlig_data, aes(y = goals_minus_xg)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Goals Minus xG",
    y = "Goals Scored per Match - xG per Match"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

{r}
superlig_data %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(goals_minus_xg))) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10) %>%
  mutate(team_season = paste(common_name, season, sep = " - ")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(team_season, goals_minus_xg), y = goals_minus_xg)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Largest Overperformers and Underperformers Against xG",
    x = "Team - Season",
    y = "Goals Scored per Match - xG per Match"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

Section 1 Summary:xG is positively related to actual goals scored, shots on target, and points per game. However, the relationship is not perfect because xG measures chance quality, not guaranteed goals.

<br> *** <br>

Section 2 - xG Evolution and Finishing Performance in the Süper Lig

This section analyzes how expected goals evolved across recent Süper Lig seasons and examines the relationship between xG and actual goal-scoring performance.

2.1 Evolution of xG Accuracy

{r}
seasonal_xg_accuracy <- superlig_data %>%
  group_by(season_short) %>%
  summarize(
    correlation = cor(xg_for_avg_overall, goals_scored_per_match, use = "complete.obs"),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

seasonal_xg_accuracy %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = season_short, y = correlation, group = 1)) +
  geom_line(color = "purple", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "purple") +
  expand_limits(y = 0) +
  xlab("Season") +
  ylab("Correlation") +
  ggtitle("Evolution of xG Accuracy by Season")

Analytical Insight: The relationship between xG and actual goals becomes stronger in recent seasons. However, the correlation never reaches 1 because xG is a probability-based metric, not a perfect prediction of goals.

2.2 Why xG is not Perfect

{r}
last3seasons_data <- superlig_data %>%
  filter(season_short %in% c("23-24", "24-25", "25-26"))

last3seasons_data %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = finishing_diff)) +
  geom_histogram(
    binwidth = 0.10,
    fill = "darkorange",
    color = "black"
  ) +
  xlab("Goals per Match - xG per Match") +
  ylab("Frequency") +
  ggtitle("Finishing Difference Distribution Last 3 Seasons")

Analytical Insight: Some teams score more goals than their xG suggests, while others score fewer. Player finishing ability, goalkeeper saves, defensive pressure, and luck can all create differences between expected and actual goals.

2.3 Shot Quality Evolution

{r}
seasonal_shot_quality <- superlig_data %>%
  group_by(season_short) %>%
  summarize(
    average_shot_quality = mean(shot_quality, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

seasonal_shot_quality %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = season_short, y = average_shot_quality, group = 1)) +
  geom_line(color = "darkblue", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "darkblue", size = 3) +
  expand_limits(y = 0) +
  xlab("Season") +
  ylab("Average xG per Shot") +
  ggtitle("Evolution of Shot Quality")

Analytical Insight: This analysis helps us understand whether teams are creating better chances or simply taking more shots.

2.4 Home Advantage and xG

{r}
home_away_xg <- superlig_data %>%
  group_by(season_short) %>%
  summarize(
    home_xg = mean(xg_for_avg_home, na.rm = TRUE),
    away_xg = mean(xg_for_avg_away, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

home_away_long <- home_away_xg %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(home_xg, away_xg),
    names_to = "location",
    values_to = "xg"
  )

home_away_long %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = season_short, y = xg, color = location, group = location)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  expand_limits(y = 0) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "home_xg" = "navy",
      "away_xg" = "darkred"
    )
  ) +
  xlab("Season") +
  ylab("Average xG per Match") +
  ggtitle("Home vs Away xG")

Analytical Insight: Home teams generally generate higher xG than away teams, suggesting that home advantage still plays an important offensive role.

Section 2 Key Takeaways:* Expected goals has a strong relationship with actual goals, but it is not a perfect predictor.* Finishing difference helps identify teams that score more or less than expected.* Shot quality analysis shows whether teams are creating efficient chances.* Home advantage remains important in attacking performance.

<br> *** <br>

Section 3: xG and Success in the Süper Lig

The main objective of this section is to determine what truly drives success in the Turkish Süper Lig.

{r}
analysis_data <- superlig_data %>%
  mutate(
    Season = season_short,
    xGD = xg_for_avg_overall - xg_against_avg_overall,
    is_champion = ifelse(league_position == 1, "Champion", "Other Teams")
  )

3.1 What Drives Success? Offense vs. Defense

{r}
correlation_df <- analysis_data %>%
  summarise(
    xG_Points = cor(xg_for_avg_overall, points_per_game, use = "complete.obs"),
    xGA_Points = cor(xg_against_avg_overall, points_per_game, use = "complete.obs"),
    xGD_Points = cor(xGD, points_per_game, use = "complete.obs")
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "Metric", values_to = "Correlation") %>%
  mutate(Strength = abs(Correlation))

ggplot(correlation_df, aes(x = reorder(Metric, Strength), y = Correlation, fill = Metric)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = round(Correlation, 2)),
    hjust = ifelse(correlation_df$Correlation > 0, -0.2, 1.2),
    size = 5,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "xG_Points" = "#27ae60",
    "xGA_Points" = "#e74c3c",
    "xGD_Points" = "#2980b9"
  )) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-0.8, 1.2)) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "What Drives Success in the Süper Lig?",
    subtitle = "Correlation between Points per Game and xG Metrics",
    x = "Performance Metrics",
    y = "Correlation Coefficient"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

Analytical Insight: Expected Goal Difference is one of the strongest indicators of league success because it combines attacking production and defensive control.

3.2 Champion Profiles

{r}
mean_xg <- mean(analysis_data$xg_for_avg_overall, na.rm = TRUE)
mean_xga <- mean(analysis_data$xg_against_avg_overall, na.rm = TRUE)

ggplot(analysis_data, aes(x = xg_against_avg_overall, y = xg_for_avg_overall)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = is_champion, size = is_champion), alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean_xg, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean_xga, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50", alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Champion" = "#f1c40f", "Other Teams" = "#2c3e50")) +
  scale_size_manual(values = c("Champion" = 3.5, "Other Teams" = 1.5)) +
  scale_x_reverse() +
  facet_wrap(~ Season, ncol = 4) +
  labs(
    title = "Süper Lig Team Profiles by Season",
    x = "xGA per Match Lower is Better",
    y = "xG per Match",
    color = "Status",
    size = "Status"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

Analytical Insight: Champions usually combine above-average attacking production with strong defensive control.

3.3 Champion vs Challengers

{r}
top4_data <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(league_position <= 4) %>%
  mutate(Position = case_when(
    league_position == 1 ~ "1st Champion",
    league_position == 2 ~ "2nd",
    league_position == 3 ~ "3rd",
    league_position == 4 ~ "4th"
  )) %>%
  mutate(Position = factor(Position, levels = c("1st Champion", "2nd", "3rd", "4th")))

ggplot(top4_data, aes(x = Season, y = xGD, fill = Position)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge", width = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "1st Champion" = "#f1c40f",
    "2nd" = "#bdc3c7",
    "3rd" = "#cd7f32",
    "4th" = "#34495e"
  )) +
  labs(
    title = "Champion vs Challengers",
    subtitle = "xGD Comparison",
    x = "Season",
    y = "xGD per Match",
    fill = "League Finish"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

Final Insight: xG and xGD are powerful indicators of team strength, but football outcomes are still influenced by finishing skill, goalkeeper performance, tactical context, and randomness.
